title: HubSpot AEO vs. Semrush AI Visibility: Which is right for your team?
content:
If you’re comparing HubSpot AEO vs Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit, I tested both for you as a marketing and AEO practitioner myself and will share my detailed review.
To run the experiment, I used one of the niche websites in my portfolio (a golf website) that hasn’t yet been optimized for AI search. Below, you’ll get screenshots and information from my personal experience testing both HubSpot AEO and Semrush One (which includes Semrush’s AI Visibility features). Then, I’ll walk you through the pros and cons of both AEO tools and help you pick the best one based on your team’s needs.
But first, let me demystify AEO, GEO, and all things AI visibility so we’re working from the same definitions.
AEO stands for answer engine optimization , and it’s the practice of creating and modifying online content so that it is more likely to be mentioned and cited by AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. You might also hear people refer to AEO as GEO ( generative engine optimization ) or AI SEO, but here at HubSpot, we stick with the term AEO.
AEO matters because, as AI becomes more popular, people are turning to answer engines to do their buyer research, in addition to Google. In 2026, nearly half of U.S. adults use AI chatbots, up from one-third in 2024, according to the Pew Research Center . Further, Pew found that 60% of American adults read the AI-generated summaries at the top of search results, while only 30% say they do not. Brands that learn and leverage AEO will gain a competitive advantage.
AI visibility is an umbrella term for the metrics that measure how your brand shows up in AI search, including share of voice, sentiment, citations, and mentions. It matters because this is how marketers and SEOs track their AEO progress.
Pro tip: To get a baseline snapshot of your AI visibility, use the free AI Search Grader tool.
Prompts are to AEO what keywords are to SEO. Prompts are the phrases that users type into answer engines to get information about their query. Marketers use AEO tools like HubSpot AEO to track the prompts their brands should show up for.
Citations are the websites that the AI consulted to generate its answer. They may or may not be linked.
Coverage is shorthand for “answer engine coverage,” which refers to which LLMs the AEO tool tracks. For example, HubSpot AEO covers ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity.
First, let me clarify the product naming and tiers, so you understand which one you need to buy. HubSpot AEO is available to purchase on its own, without another HubSpot subscription. Additionally, AEO is the name of the CRM-connected product included within Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise.
Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit is available to purchase on its own or as an add-on to an existing Semrush subscription. Semrush SEO + AI Search is also known as Semrush One , and it’s the bundled product with SEO and AEO features.
This article (and the quick comparison table below) primarily compares HubSpot AEO and Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit (the products available for purchase on their own). But I’ll also include additional information about AEO in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise and Semrush One (the integrated/bundled products).
HubSpot AEO uses the official APIs of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity to run your tracked prompts daily and show you the actual AI responses.
Users can manually add prompts to HubSpot AEO or get suggestions based on the company info they provide during onboarding. Or, if they’re using AEO in Marketing Hub Pro+, users can get AI-powered suggestions that draw upon context from the CRM data. The advantage of this is that the suggestions get smarter over time as the CRM learns more about your business.
HubSpot AEO’s dashboard shows a detailed citation analysis, including owned citation rate versus competitors, citations by content type, and citations by channel.
HubSpot AEO users can get a sense for how their brand mentions are doing by going to the Dashboard tab and viewing the brand visibility score to see how often their brand is mentioned for tracked prompts, and brand visibility over time to track progress. For more granular data, they can go to the Prompt tabs and click on each individual prompt to see if their brand was mentioned in that answer and on which of the three answer engines it was mentioned.
Semrush differs from HubSpot AEO in the way it fetches answers. Instead of sending the prompts live to every answer engine every time, it has a pre-existing proprietary database of over 289 million prompts that it pulls from. The prompt database is updated daily.
Users can manually add prompts or use the synthetic prompts that Semrush suggests based on the user’s submitted domain and location. If a user manually adds prompts for tracking, then Semrush runs it live to see what answers get fetched.
Unlike AEO in HubSpot Marketing Hub Pro+, Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit does not have a CRM, so it cannot use your business context to personalize prompts like HubSpot can.
I found it confusing to try to locate my brand’s citations within Semrush’s AI Visibility dashboard. Instead of a dedicated Citations tab, Semrush has a few places where you can find info on how often AI cites your domain. Users can find it under AI Visibility > Visibility Overview > Citations, which shows how many AI answers a domain gets cited in. Scroll down to Cited Pages, and you can see the exact URLs on your website that are getting cited by AI.
Under AI Visibility > Competitor Research > Sources > Missing, you can see which third-party websites are driving your competitors’ AI visibility. These are opportunities for outreach to gain inclusion on those third-party sites.
Semrush users can go to AI Visibility > Visibility Overview and see their AI visibility score next to how mention counts are trending over time. On the same page, brand mentions are broken down by LLM distribution, country, topic, and prompt.
Winner: HubSpot For Content Creation, Semrush For Technical Optimization
This section covers how easy it is to take action on AEO insights provided by HubSpot AEO vs Semrush AI Visibility.
Both tools provide recommendations tailored to your brand, based on what answer engines are already saying about it. However, they differ in their level of detail. HubSpot AEO provides prescriptive recommendations on blog posts you should create, providing a brief with a suggested title, target audience, summary, and primary and secondary keywords.
Semrush provides more high-level directional guidance, such as adjusting your brand voice or adding certain content design elements. It doesn’t give detailed guidance on actual blog posts to create — at least, not within its AI Visibility Toolkit. You might have to purchase the Content Toolkit add-on for that.
Unlike HubSpot, Semrush doesn’t have a CMS or a CRM, so it lacks the unified path from insight to action that HubSpot has. Moving from suggestion to implementation will be more of a hassle, as you’ll need a separate tool for publishing. To get from insight to content creation with HubSpot, you’ll need Marketing Hub Pro/Enterprise (which includes AEO features and a CRM) or HubSpot for Marketers (which includes AEO features, a CRM, and a CMS). To create content with Semrush, you’ll need the Content Toolkit add-on.
As for technical optimization, both tools will alert you to AI-specific technical issues, such as a robots.txt file blocking an AI crawler. However, Semrush provides a dedicated AI Search Health score within its deeper, traditional Site Audit tool, making it stronger for overall technical SEO.
The fastest way to turn visibility gaps into content updates is to use HubSpot for Marketers , which combines Marketing Hub, Content Hub, and AEO to help you create answer engine-friendly content fast based on your actual CRM data. Subscribers to HubSpot for Marketers or Marketing Hub Professional/Enterprise can use Content Agent to generate research-backed blog posts based on AEO recommendations.
As a writer, I’m always going to advocate for keeping humans in the loop, especially when writing AEO content. If you are going to use AI, use AI that has the proper context about your brand; otherwise, your outputs will be generic. For example, subscribers to Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise get AEO feature access that draws upon CRM data to give more contextualized prompt suggestions based on your actual business.
Here are a couple of the best places AI can speed up AEO tasks:
Winner: HubSpot. HubSpot’s advantage is its native integration with its Smart CRM as well as its marketing and content tools. Using AEO within a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription grants you the ability to own the AEO process end-to-end, from AEO insight to published content. There’s also closed-loop reporting because it all happens within the HubSpot platform.
That CRM connection means you can get personalized prompt suggestions based on your business context within HubSpot. HubSpot also has integrations with Google Analytics and Google Search Console, as well as more than 1,000 other integrations available in the HubSpot Marketplace .
Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit natively integrates with the Semrush SEO platform, which is useful if you’re already using it for SEO. It also provides integrations with Google Analytics and Google Search Console. Semrush has deeper features for search engine optimization than HubSpot does. However, Semrush lacks the CRM prompt grounding and personalization that HubSpot has. Semrush’s third-party integrations include WordPress, Trello, Google Docs, and Facebook.
Winner: HubSpot. Of the two, I found HubSpot AEO the easiest to use. The onboarding was substantially better, with more guidance and personalization. Semrush dropped me right into my dashboard after I entered my domain.
HubSpot’s UI is intuitive and simple, making it easy to navigate. That’s not a knock against Semrush, though. If Semrush feels complicated, it’s just because it has such a wide range of features, so it takes more getting used to. If simplicity and ease are your main goals, then HubSpot AEO is for you. But if feature robustness matters more, try Semrush.
Non-SEOs (marketers especially) will get the most value at the fastest rate by using HubSpot AEO and completing the guided onboarding process. It’s extremely user-friendly and made for marketers. For example, HubSpot AEO allows you to tailor your prompts based on different ICPs.
Best for: Getting a high-level snapshot of your AI visibility before you deep dive into advanced AEO tools
HubSpot AEO does not have a free plan, but HubSpot does offer a free tool that helps marketers get a snapshot of their AI readiness. AI Search Grader gives marketers a free point-in-time report of their brand’s AI visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity — perfect for getting a baseline. The report is based on the LLMs’ training data, so it’s useful for knowing where you stand when you first get started on AEO. But to track your brand’s target prompts and actual progress, you’ll need to upgrade to HubSpot AEO.
Start by getting your baseline using the free AI Search Grader . Just enter your domain, and AI Search Grader will give you a one-time snapshot of your AI visibility based on existing training data for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. It’ll score your brand on sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market competition.
Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit does not have a free plan, but the free Semrush plan grants access to Domain Overview to provide a snapshot of your domain’s mentions, citations, and AI visibility score. It also grants access to Site Audit, allowing you to audit up to 100 pages for technical issues that are hindering your AI visibility.
Best for: Evaluating advanced AEO tools before committing to a paid subscription
For more advanced AI visibility and continuous tracking, HubSpot AEO offers a 28-day free trial. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit ($99/mo/domain) does not offer a free trial. However, Semrush SEO + AI Search (starting at $199/mo billed monthly) does offer a seven-day free trial .
Setting up on both is incredibly easy — all you need to do is enter your domain. Then, for HubSpot AEO, it’ll guide you through onboarding, asking for more details about your business so it can provide personalized prompt suggestions.
Marketers serious about AEO quickly outgrow free plans and trials. Once you’ve taken advantage of free trials for evaluation purposes, you’re ready to commit to a paid subscription for long-term tracking and expedited AEO progress.
HubSpot AEO can be purchased on its own for just $50/mo, granting you 25 prompts that it tracks daily. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit can be purchased on its own for $99/mo/domain, also allowing you to track 25 prompts.
Personally, I like to pilot software I’m considering side by side. So, I’d recommend signing up for HubSpot AEO’s free 28-day trial at the same time that you sign up for Semrush One’s 7-day free trial. Then, spend the next week using them side by side and comparing their strengths and weaknesses.
Use the same domain to get a true apples-to-apples comparison of how each tool approaches the AEO process.
From there, I’d create a few pieces of content based on HubSpot AEO’s recommendations and Semrush’s recommendations. Think of this as split testing. Create a spreadsheet of the content that was based on HubSpot and a separate tab for the content that was based on Semrush.
AEO efforts, similar to SEO work, take time to show impact. Track both pieces of content over the next three months. Track these metrics: citations, mentions, prompts. Note: Because the free trial for HubSpot AEO ends after 28 days and Semrush One after seven days, you’ll have to upgrade to the paid version of HubSpot AEO ($50/mo) and then the paid version of the standalone Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit ($99/mo/domain).
At the end of your three-month pilot, see which tool ended up giving you content recommendations that moved the needle for your AI visibility. In addition to that, take note of which tool was genuinely most helpful and easy to use for your team.
Best for: Enterprise teams wanting to automate the AEO content creation process (while maintaining human-in-the-loop approval)
Best for: Mid-market to enterprise teams needing technical optimizations and AI traffic attribution
Pricing: Starts at $250/mo for four answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Microsoft Copilot)
Best for: Teams already using Ahrefs for SEO, or those focused on AI visibility on social media
If you’re already using Profound, Scrunch, or Ahrefs, you can still add HubSpot AEO by purchasing it on its own. This will grant you access to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity data, as well as HubSpot’s prompt suggestions and content recommendations. To get CRM-powered suggestions that are personalized based on your business context, upgrade to Marketing Hub Pro+ or HubSpot for Marketers.
Subscribers of HubSpot for Marketers (Marketing Hub Pro+ and Content Hub Pro+ bundled) can own the AEO content creation process end-to-end by getting the AEO recommendation, clicking a button to create content with Content Agent, and then tracking that content’s URL to see its impact on AEO — all in one place. This avoids stack sprawl and governance gaps, enabling a centralized dashboard for AEO insights and actions.
Yes, in fact, using Semrush for SEO and HubSpot for AEO is the recommended approach. Semrush has deep expertise and functionality for keyword research, backlink tracking, and competitor research, while HubSpot provides the unique CRM-connected prompt suggestions that help your business stand out. The CRM-based prompt suggestions are available only for subscribers of Marketing Hub Professional/Enterprise or HubSpot for Marketers.
Alternatively, if you’re using Semrush for SEO and don’t want to pay the additional $99 to add its AI Visibility Toolkit, HubSpot AEO is available for purchase on its own for just $50, which brings down your total cost of ownership.
AEO success ultimately depends on whether your AEO efforts are building your pipeline. So, beyond visibility scores, you need to connect your AEO content to business impact. For this, I recommend HubSpot Marketing Hub Enterprise because then you’ll get AEO features and multi-touch attribution that can tell you how your AEO efforts are tied to actual deals in your pipeline.
The best way to get cited in AI answers is to learn answer engine optimization (AEO), which includes tactics such as creating answer-first content, improving your off-site reputation, ensuring your site has no technical issues, and using a dedicated AEO tool. For more details, check out HubSpot’s AEO guide .
First, a caveat: Good AEO relies on a solid SEO foundation. So, once you’ve got a solid SEO foundation in place, prioritize AEO over traditional SEO if you have not yet optimized your site for answer engines. I recommend this because AI search behavior is growing fast , and it takes time for AEO content to compound. So starting on AEO now will pay off in the future.

title: AI SEO tools that fit your growth stack
content:
AI SEO tools have matured quickly. What started as a novelty layer atop existing keyword tools has become a full-fledged category, helping improve everything from research to AI search visibility.
Growth teams now have real choices about where AI can provide the most value across the SEO workflow. More than 90% of marketing teams now use AI in their workflows — but having AI in your stack and having the right AI in your stack are two different things.
This guide breaks down AI SEO tools by job-to-be-done, explains how to evaluate them against your growth stack, and provides a practical framework for automating SEO without sacrificing quality.
AI SEO tools help with keyword research, clustering, content creation, optimization, audits, internal linking, and AI visibility. They are software platforms that use machine learning and large language models to automate, accelerate, or enhance specific tasks within the SEO workflow.
They accelerate SEO judgment by reducing the time required to apply it at scale. The core jobs AI SEO tools are built to do include the following.
The value AI adds to each of these jobs varies. Research and clustering, technical auditing, and on-page optimization tend to see the highest ROI from automation simply because they’re repetitive, high-volume, and rule-governed tasks. Content drafting and strategy work require more human judgment to be effective.
Choosing the right AI SEO tool boils down to matching capability to context. Here’s how to evaluate your options.
A team focused on topical authority needs different tools than one focused on improving crawl efficiency or scaling blog output. Before comparing tools, be specific about what job you need done most urgently.
Some AI SEO tools are built for specialists. Screaming Frog, for instance, delivers extraordinary technical depth, but requires comfort with crawl data interpretation. Other tools, like HubSpot’s built-in SEO tools, are designed for marketers who need actionable recommendations without a technical SEO background.
If a team publishes five pieces per month, a heavy automation stack creates overhead without enough output to justify it. If a team publishes 50+ pieces per month, automation for briefing, clustering, and on-page optimization compounds quickly.
Disconnected tools mean disconnected data. An AI SEO tool that plugs directly into your CMS allows recommendations to be acted on in context, not in a separate dashboard. A tool that connects to your CRM means SEO performance can be tied to pipeline, not just traffic.
HubSpot’s SEO tools are built into Marketing Hub, which means topic and keyword suggestions, page optimization recommendations, and performance analytics all live in the same system as your content, contacts, and conversion data. This integration removes friction and helps growth teams connect SEO efforts to revenue.
AI-assisted drafts and automated recommendations require human review especially for brands where tone, accuracy, or compliance matter. Choose tools that build review into the workflow, not ones that assume automation equals publishing.
Vanity metrics are easy to track. What’s harder — and more valuable — is understanding whether SEO effort is actually driving qualified traffic, pipeline, or revenue. Prioritize tools with reporting that connects organic performance to business outcomes.
Pro tip: Before evaluating tools, make sure the foundation is solid. The HubSpot Complete SEO Starter Pack includes an on-page SEO template, a search intent and research template, and a 21 SEO myths ebook to help build a reliable SEO baseline — free to download.
There’s no single AI SEO tool that handles every job well. The best approach is to match tools to specific workflow stages. Below is a breakdown by job type, with notes on where each tool excels.
Keyword research used to mean building a spreadsheet of terms one by one. AI-powered research tools now surface related terms, group them by topic cluster, and prioritize opportunities based on difficulty and intent in minutes.
HubSpot’s SEO tools are built directly into Marketing Software , which makes them useful for teams that want research to flow directly into content creation and publishing. The topic cluster tool helps teams identify pillar topics, map supporting content, and visualize how pages relate, so internal linking and content planning happen in the same system.
What I like: The native CMS connection means keyword insights don’t stay in a separate dashboard. A recommendation made in the SEO tool can be acted on immediately in the page editor.That integration removes real friction while the CRM connection means you can actually measure whether that organic traffic converts.
Best for: Growth teams already using HubSpot CMS or HubSpot Smart CRM who want research, content strategy, and performance measurement in one place.
SparkToro is used for audience research and content planning inputs, and it’s an audience intelligence tool that answers a question most SEO tools don’t touch: where does your target audience actually spend their time online?
Rather than starting with keywords and working backward to an audience, SparkToro starts with the audience and surfaces the podcasts they listen to, the websites they read, the YouTube channels they watch, the social accounts they follow, and the topics they search for.
What I like: SparkToro answers a question that keyword research can’t — not what people are searching for, but where they’re paying attention.
Best for: Content strategists, digital PR teams, and demand gen marketers who want to ground their channel and distribution decisions in audience data rather than convention or guesswork.
Pricing: Free plan available. Paid plans from $38/month
Keyword Insights is used for keyword clustering and content brief creation, which saves significant time when building topic maps for content programs. Upload a seed list, and it groups terms that can realistically be targeted on a single page versus those that need their own content.
What I like: The clustering logic is genuinely useful. It’s grouping by whether Google treats keywords as interchangeable on the SERP, not just grouping by theme.
Best for: Content teams building out topical clusters who have existing keyword lists to work with.
AlsoAsked pulls directly from Google’s “People Also Ask” data to map how questions branch and relate from any seed keyword. The output is a visual tree that shows how one question leads to another, reflecting how Google actually understands the semantic relationships between topics.
What I like: The data comes straight from Google, which means you’re seeing exactly what real users are being shown not what an algorithm guesses they might ask. For FAQ-heavy content and featured snippet targeting, that accuracy is hard to replicate with other tools.
Best for: Content strategists and SEO teams building topic clusters, content briefs, or FAQ sections who want to ground their planning in real search behavior rather than keyword assumptions.
Content briefs give writers everything they need to create well-optimized content without starting from scratch. AI-assisted drafting speeds up production by generating structured outlines or full drafts based on top-ranking content and search intent.
HubSpot Content Hub is a full-stack content marketing platform built around the entire content lifecycle, from ideation to publishing to performance tracking. The AI assistant can generate drafts, repurpose existing content, and suggest structure based on SEO and audience inputs, all within the CMS, so there’s no context-switching between where content is created and where it’s published.
Every piece of content connects to the CRM, SEO data, conversion analytics, and the rest of Marketing Hub . That means AI-generated content is created inside the same system where you track who’s reading it, what they do next, and whether it actually drives the pipeline.
What I like: The integration with the rest of Marketing Hub means AI drafts can be immediately reviewed, edited, and published. Performance can be tracked against the same audience and conversion data the team already uses.
Best for: Teams running content and marketing in HubSpot who want drafting, optimization, and publishing in one workflow.
SurferSEO is used for on-page optimization and content refresh workflows. Surfer’s Content Editor uses AI to analyze top-ranking pages for a given keyword and generate a brief that includes suggested headings, NLP terms, and word count targets. Writers can use the editor in real time to see a relevance score update as they write.
What I like: The real-time feedback loop during writing is genuinely useful for keeping content on-target without constant tab-switching. It’s one of the more intuitive brief-to-draft tools available.
Best for: Content writers and editors who want a structured brief and real-time optimization guidance in one tool.
Frase is built around a research-to-brief-to-draft workflow. It aggregates information from top-ranking pages on a topic, generates a brief, and offers an AI writing assistant that can fill in sections based on the research. It’s useful for teams producing alot of informational content.
What I like: The research aggregation is fast. Frase reduces the time to a working draft significantly for teams building FAQ-heavy or comparison content.
Best for: Teams producing informational content at scale who want research and drafting in a single tool.
On-page optimization is where AI tools have arguably had the most immediate impact. Scoring pages against top-ranking competitors, surfacing missing concepts, and flagging structural issues are tasks that AI handles quickly and consistently.
Clearscope grades content based on how thoroughly it covers a topic compared to top-ranking pages. It surfaces related terms, grades the overall comprehensiveness of the content, and integrates with Google Docs and WordPress for in-editor optimization.
What I like: The grading system is clear, and the term suggestions focus on topic relevance rather than semantic matching alone.
Best for: Content teams running systematic refresh programs across large content libraries.
MarketMuse builds a content inventory and scores each piece based on topical depth relative to competitors. Its AI can identify content gaps, generate briefs for missing subtopics, and prioritize which pages to optimize first based on difficulty and authority. It’s more of a strategic tool than a page-level editor.
What I like : MarketMuse helps teams quickly identify the highest-priority gaps across an entire content library. It prevents duplication and focuses effort where it will have the most strategic impact rather than optimizing ad hoc.
Best for: Enterprise and mid-market teams managing content libraries of 100+ pages who need a strategic, site-wide view of content gaps rather than just page-level editing.
Technical SEO — crawl efficiency, site speed, structured data, canonicalization, crawl errors — requires tooling that can read the site the way a search engine would.
Screaming Frog is used for technical crawling and issue discovery. It crawls websites and returns a comprehensive dataset covering response codes, redirect chains, duplicate content, missing metadata, hreflang, schema markup issues, Core Web Vitals, and much more.
What I like: This tool provides unmatched crawl data depth at its price point. The AI integration lets teams run content quality checks or custom extraction prompts at scale during a crawl, without building a separate workflow.
Best for: Technical SEOs and developers managing site health at scale especially before or after a major content push, site migration, or CMS change.
Pricing: Free (up to 500 URLs) or $279/year for unlimited
Sitebulb is a visual-first technical auditing tool that presents crawl data in a more accessible format. It includes AI-generated audit summaries that explain issues in plain language and prioritize fixes by estimated impact.
What I like: The visual audit reports make it easier to brief developers on technical issues without needing to export and reformat raw data. For agencies presenting findings to clients, that alone saves significant time.
Best for: Agencies and in-house teams that need to report technical findings to stakeholders who don’t have technical expertise.
Internal linking improves crawl efficiency, distributes page authority, and signals to search engines how topics relate. Identifying the right opportunities manually across hundreds of pages is impractical. AI tools automate the discovery.
Ahrefs is best known as a backlink and keyword research platform, but its Site Audit and internal link reporting tools make it a strong addition to any site structure workflow. For teams already using Ahrefs for competitive research, the internal linking data is right there — no separate tool required.
What I like: Having internal link auditing in the same platform removes a context switch for teams already in Ahrefs for keyword and competitive research. The Best By Links report is particularly useful. It’s a fast way to identify which pages are already earning authority and make sure they’re linking to the content that needs it most.
Best for: SEO teams already using Ahrefs who want internal linking insights alongside their broader keyword and backlink workflow, without adding another tool.
Link Whisperer is a WordPress plugin that uses AI to suggest and insert internal links as content is written or edited, with site-level reporting for orphaned pages, broken links, and link structure analysis.
What I like: Link Whisper removes the manual work of internal linking without requiring a strategic overhaul. The GSC integration surfaces the terms Google already associates with your pages as linking targets, which makes suggestions more accurate than a pure keyword match.
Best for : WordPress sites with 50+ published pages where manual internal linking becomes a bottleneck. Not suited for non-WordPress sites.
Answer engine optimization tools focus on improving visibility in AI-generated answers, citations, and brand mentions. While SEO focuses on ranking in traditional search results, AEO focuses on appearing in AI-generated answers from systems like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Bing Copilot.
AEO and SEO are different disciplines, but complementary ones. Teams that optimize for both are building durable visibility for the channels where buyers are increasingly going to find answers.
HubSpot AEO helps assess current AI search visibility, helping teams understand where their brand appears in AI-generated answers and why. It surfaces which pages are being cited, which queries are triggering citations, and where visibility gaps exist across AI engines — and it does all of that inside the same platform where teams are already tracking SEO, content, and pipeline.
For demand generation leaders being asked to show how content investment connects to pipeline, AEO visibility metrics — citations, share of AI answers, coverage by topic — are becoming a required reporting layer alongside traditional SEO metrics.
What I like: The combination of SEO and AEO in a single platform means teams can see the full picture of how their content is being found both in traditional search and in the AI-generated answers where purchase decisions increasingly begin. That integration is what makes the data actionable rather than just interesting.
Best for: Growth teams that want to measure and optimize for both traditional SEO and AI search visibility without managing two separate reporting systems. It’s especially useful for teams already on Marketing Hub who want to add AI visibility tracking without adding another tool.
Pricing: $50 per month as a standalone tool or included in Marketing Hub Pro and Enterprise editions
HubSpot AEO Grader is a free diagnostic tool that evaluates how AI engines currently characterize your brand based on their training data. Rather than auditing your website, it assesses your brand across five dimensions — sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market position — and returns a score out of 100 with written interpretation of the results across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini.
It’s a useful first step for teams evaluating content positioning in AI-generated answers without full commitment to an audit. The output is specific enough to act on, and it takes minutes rather than hours.
Pro tip: Run the AEO Grader before building your AI visibility roadmap. It’s a fast way to understand where the biggest gaps are without committing to a full audit. The prioritized output gives you a defensible starting point for deciding where to focus first.
Free Resource: Before diving deeper into SEO and AEO tooling, make sure the foundation is solid. The HubSpot Complete SEO Starter Pack includes an on-page SEO template, a search intent and research template, and a 21 SEO myths ebook to help build a reliable baseline — free to download.
Automation creates scale. But poorly configured automation also creates scale for thin content, mismatched intent, and inconsistent brand voice. Here’s how to build an automated SEO workflow that maintains quality at every stage.
Start by generating a large seed list of keywords either manually, through customer research, or using a dedicated keyword research tool like Semrush. If you’re already using HubSpot, HubSpot’s SEO tools can surface topic and keyword suggestions based on relevance and competition to help inform your content strategy.
Then batch-upload that list into a clustering tool (Keyword Insights works well here) to group terms by topic and intent. The goal at this stage is to understand your full topical landscape before committing to content priorities. Clustering first prevents the common mistake of creating multiple pages that compete with each other.
Once keywords are clustered, map each cluster to one of three content types:
This mapping becomes the architecture for your editorial calendar, not just a list of keywords to target.
Document which clusters represent existing content opportunities versus net-new content opportunities. That distinction determines where you use refresh workflows versus new production workflows.
AI drafts are useful when they’re used as a first draft, not a final one. Generate a draft from a brief, then treat it as a structured research document that needs a human layer. Take time for:
The mistake is publishing AI drafts without that layer. The content technically exists, but it doesn’t build authority, and it doesn’t say anything a search engine couldn’t find elsewhere. The human layer is what makes content worth citing.
Every content workflow that uses AI assistance needs a human review checkpoint. This isn’t optional. Make it explicit in your SOP. Define:
For teams managing high content volume, a checklist-based review speeds things up while maintaining standards. Build the checklist once, use it every time.
Publish-and-forget is a visibility leak. A quarterly or biannual content audit — using HubSpot’s SEO recommendations to surface technical and on-page issues, or Semrush’s content audit tool for deeper cannibalization and competitive analysis — helps identify pages that have lost ranking or become factually outdated. Schedule audits like you schedule production.
Every content audit should include an internal linking pass. Consider:
Internal linking is one of the highest-ROI, lowest-cost SEO tasks available — and it’s consistently underdone. Automating the discovery makes it easier to stay on top of it without blocking the production workflow.
AI search optimization tools are software platforms that use artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve how search engines discover, index, and rank content. AI SEO tools assist SEO teams in completing existing SEO tasks more efficiently, while AEO tools address a newer visibility layer in AI-generated answer surfaces.
Small businesses benefit most from tools that are simple to use and don’t require dedicated technical expertise. HubSpot’s SEO tools , built into Marketing Hub, offer topic and keyword suggestions, on-page recommendations, and performance reporting in a single interface that doesn’t require an SEO background to use effectively. The priority for small businesses should be coverage at the critical workflow stages — research, on-page, and technical — rather than maximum tool count.
AI-assisted content that includes original insights, accurate information, proper structure, and genuine expertise can rank and perform well. The issue isn’t that AI writes the first draft. Problems occur when AI drafts are published without meaningful human review, fact-checking, or original perspective. Google’s quality guidance focuses on the usefulness and expertise of the final piece, not the process used to create it. Teams that use AI to accelerate production and then invest the human effort in quality can produce high-ranking content efficiently.
Start with a baseline before introducing new tools: organic traffic, ranking positions for target keywords, and conversion rate from organic. After implementation, track those same metrics — but also look at operational efficiency metrics. The ROI case for AI SEO tools usually reduces the number of hours spent on high-volume, repetitive tasks and increases organic traffic gains from content that gets optimized and refreshed more systematically than manual workflows allow.
Competitive commercial terms, comparison content, and anything referencing data, statistics, or tools should be reviewed every six months at a minimum. Informational content on slower-moving topics can run on an annual review cycle.
The practical approach is to use an AI SEO audit tool — HubSpot’s SEO recommendations, Semrush’s content audit, or similar — to flag pages that have dropped in ranking or accumulated significant outdated content, and use that signal to prioritize the refresh queue rather than working through an arbitrary calendar.
AI SEO tools are a practical requirement for staying competitive in a space where the volume and complexity of SEO work have outpaced what manual processes can handle. The best approach is to build a stack where each tool handles the job it does best:
The goal is automation that frees up resources for human judgment, expertise, and original thinking — qualities that search engines and AI systems reward.
HubSpot’s SEO tools cover the topic suggestions, optimization, and reporting workflow natively within Marketing Hub, making them a strong anchor for teams that want fewer disconnected dashboards and tighter alignment between SEO performance and revenue. For teams ready to look beyond traditional search, HubSpot AEO adds the AI visibility layer that lets the same team track citations and presence in AI-generated answers alongside organic rankings.
